title: Select first-version scope after requirements review
goal: Ensure the requirements interview produces a reviewed requirements brief before asking the user to choose features for the hackathon's first version.
in_scope: Update the project-local requirements-interview skill to separate requirements discovery and review from first-version feature selection.

Require the agent to synthesize and present the requirements brief, including confirmed information, assumptions, and open questions, and incorporate the user's corrections before moving to scope selection.
After requirements review, map relevant features by independent, cross-cutting, and prerequisite-dependent relationships.
Present a concrete minimal MVP recommendation and relevant scope alternatives with tradeoffs, then ask the user which features belong in the first version while preserving necessary prerequisites.
Avoid asking vague or premature questions such as which direction is closest to the hackathon first version during requirements discovery.
Preserve the rule that reviewing requirements or choosing MVP scope does not approve implementation.
out_of_scope: Changing the harness CLI or feature registry schema.
Implementing any product feature being discussed in a requirements interview.
acceptance_criteria: The skill clearly separates requirements discovery, requirements brief review, and first-version scope selection in that order.
The requirements brief is shown to the user and revised for corrections before the agent asks which features belong in the first version.
Feature mapping happens after requirements review and identifies independent, cross-cutting, and prerequisite-dependent capabilities.
The agent makes a concrete minimal MVP recommendation, explains relevant tradeoffs, and asks the user to confirm or adjust the feature set.
The workflow avoids asking the user to choose a vague product direction as a proxy for first-version scope during requirements discovery.
MVP scope confirmation is explicitly kept separate from per-feature implementation approval.
